clue.text: Offensive person's secure trade to grab everything

parts.note: to hedge a trade is to secure it against loss with an offsetting bet
to hog is to take everything for yourself

explanation.surface: A rude trader protects deals by grabbing everything for himself.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's stands for 'is', joining definition to wordplay. A hedgehog is a prickly creature, and figuratively a prickly person.
explanation.definitionFit: Figuratively a prickly, touchy individual is called a hedgehog, after the spiny animal that bristles at contact.

clue.text: Something bad about good indicator

indicators.note: about here means going around the outside of something, enclosing it

parts.note: a sin is a wrong act
G is the usual abbreviation for good

explanation.surface: A bad thing hinting at a good one makes a confusing pointer.
explanation.definitionFit: A sign is a mark or signal that points to or indicates something.

clue.text: Outcast runs into rainy church

indicators.note: one thing going into another means it is placed inside it

parts.note: rainy weather is wet
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs
CH is the standard abbreviation for church

explanation.surface: A homeless outsider dashes out of the rain into a church.
explanation.definitionFit: A wretch is a miserable, unfortunate person, often one cast out or shunned by society.

clue.text: Encourage burst of energy, fading at the end

indicators.note: something fading at its end loses its final part, so the last letter goes

parts.note: a spurt is a sudden burst of effort or speed

explanation.surface: An athlete is urged on, but the late burst of energy fades at the finish.
explanation.definitionFit: To spur someone is to urge them on, like a rider pressing spurs into a horse.

clue.text: Scar shown by the Devil?

definitions.meaning: first meaning, read literally: a scar is what is left of a scratch made long ago
second meaning: a traditional nickname for Satan

explanation.surface: A sinister mark displayed by Satan himself.
explanation.walkthrough: The first sense is playful, which is why the clue ends with a question mark: a scar is literally an aged scratch.
explanation.definitionFit: Old Scratch is a folk name for Satan, and taken word by word it describes a healed wound.

clue.text: Farm building, for me, lacking new block

parts.note: a sty is a pen for pigs

indicators.note: lacking something means going without it, so that letter is removed

parts.note: what is for me is mine
N is the abbreviation for new

explanation.surface: A pigsty, with nothing new for me in it, stands in my way.
explanation.definitionFit: To stymie someone is to obstruct or thwart them; the word came from a golf ball blocking the line to the hole.

clue.text: Rest will ignore a prompt

indicators.note: ignoring something means leaving it out of account, so the a is dropped

parts.note: the rest is what remains
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone resting will ignore a nudge to get up.
explanation.definitionFit: A prompt, as a noun, is something that jogs the memory, just like a reminder.

clue.text: Gloomy town dead, picking up with second amount of energy injected

indicators.note: something injected is pushed inside something else
in a down entry, picking up means the letters are lifted and read from bottom to top

parts.note: a city is a large town
D is the abbreviation for dead, as in genealogies
S is the abbreviation for second
pep is a dose of vigour

explanation.surface: A dreary, lifeless town gets a second shot of energy.
explanation.walkthrough: City and dead join and then reverse to give DYTIC; S and PEP go into its middle.
explanation.definitionFit: Dyspeptic literally means suffering indigestion, and by extension irritable and gloomy in temper.

clue.text: Respectful staff around computer department

indicators.note: one thing placed around another encloses it

parts.note: a staff is a pole or stick
IT is the department for information technology

explanation.surface: Office staff are courteous around the IT people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Staff' reads as employees, but it is a stick.
explanation.definitionFit: A polite person shows courtesy and good manners, which is being respectful.

clue.text: Spirit of destiny overlooking one part of family

indicators.note: overlooking something means missing it out, so that letter is dropped

parts.note: in Roman belief a genius is a guardian spirit governing a person's fate
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A spirit governing fate ignores one member of a family.
explanation.definitionFit: In biological classification a family is divided into several genera, so a genus is a subdivision of a family.

clue.text: Dull period around two-thirds of holiday venue

indicators.note: one thing placed around another encloses it

parts.note: a period is a span of time

indicators.note: taking two-thirds of a word keeps only that fraction of its letters

parts.note: a resort is a holiday destination; its first four of six letters are kept

explanation.surface: A boring stay spent at most of a holiday resort.
explanation.definitionFit: Something tiresome wearies you through being tedious, which is what dull means here.

clue.text: Article about English verb thesis misjudged poem with notorious verb

indicators.note: about here means going around the outside of something

parts.note: the is the definite article

indicators.note: something misjudged is got wrong, so these letters are wrongly arranged

parts.note: E is the abbreviation for English
taken as written, to be mixed with the E

explanation.surface: A grammar essay about an English verb is muddled, discussing a poem with an infamous verb.
explanation.walkthrough: THE is split around the rearranged letters. The poem is Philip Larkin's, whose first line uses a famously crude verb about what parents do to children.
explanation.definitionFit: Larkin's 1971 poem is known chiefly for its shocking opening line, built on a swear word.

clue.text: Latest drink supplier finally brought in to add energy to tournament

indicators.note: being brought into something means being placed inside it

parts.note: to stir things up is to add energy or liveliness

indicators.note: finally points to the last letter of the preceding word

parts.note: the final letter of the word supplier
a cup is a knockout competition

explanation.surface: The last round of drinks for a tournament, supplied to liven things up.
explanation.walkthrough: The supplier's last letter goes inside the phrase for adding energy, after STIR.
explanation.definitionFit: A stirrup cup was a farewell drink offered to a rider already mounted, so it is the very last drink before leaving.

clue.text: Police team bringing very cool desserts to part of school?

parts.note: V is the abbreviation for very
ices are frozen desserts
a quad is a quadrangle, a courtyard in a school or college

explanation.surface: Police officers bring ice-cream to a school yard.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark covers a quad being only one example of part of a school.
explanation.definitionFit: A vice squad is a police unit dealing with crimes such as prostitution, gambling and drugs.

clue.text: Walking style around rear of the yard offering a lot of fun

indicators.note: one thing placed around another encloses it

parts.note: a gait is a way of walking

indicators.note: the rear of a word is its final letter

parts.note: last letter of the word the
Y is the abbreviation for yard

explanation.surface: A jaunty strut around the backyard is great fun.
explanation.definitionFit: Gaiety is merriment and lively enjoyment, which is having a lot of fun.

clue.text: Put an end to providing bed in school

indicators.note: one thing in another is placed inside it

parts.note: SCH is a standard abbreviation for school
a cot is a small bed

explanation.surface: A school stops supplying beds for pupils.
explanation.definitionFit: To scotch a rumour or plan is to stop it decisively, which is to put an end to it.

clue.text: Perhaps Grandma's to threaten about one item in the will?

indicators.note: about here means going around the outside of something

parts.note: a woman's belonging, such as Grandma's, is hers: the possessive pronoun
I is the Roman numeral one
to loom is to hang menacingly over

explanation.surface: Grandma threatens to cut someone out over one item in her will.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Perhaps' marks Grandma as one example of a woman whose possession is described as her.
explanation.definitionFit: An heirloom is a valued possession handed down in a family, often bequeathed in a will.

clue.text: Recording shock about religious figure in boss's place

indicators.note: about here means going around the outside of something

parts.note: a disc is a record
a rector is a parish priest
a shock of hair is a thick mass of it

explanation.surface: A priest is captured on tape getting a shock in his boss's seat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shock' reads as a fright, but it means a mop of hair.
explanation.definitionFit: A director's chair is the folding canvas seat used on a film set by the director, who is the boss.

clue.text: Sweet song from a couple, including large contralto

indicators.note: one thing including others holds them inside it

parts.note: a duet is sung by two performers
L is the abbreviation for large
C is the abbreviation for contralto in vocal scores

explanation.surface: A sweet duet sung by a pair, one of them a big contralto.
explanation.definitionFit: Dulcet describes a sound that is sweet and soothing to hear.

clue.text: Going ahead with match, with millions coming in at the right moment

parts.note: an event still on is going ahead

indicators.note: something coming in enters the space inside another

parts.note: a tie is a cup match
M is the abbreviation for millions

explanation.surface: The big-money match is going ahead punctually.
explanation.definitionFit: Something on time arrives punctually, exactly when it should, at the right moment.

clue.text: Less-than-serious flight for fun, not entirely dreadful

indicators.note: not entirely means a word is not all there, so its last letter goes

parts.note: a flip is a short pleasure flight in an aircraft
pants is British slang for rubbish or awful

explanation.surface: A joyride flight that is not wholly terrible but not serious either.
explanation.walkthrough: In British slang something pants is very poor, and a flip is a brief joyride in a plane.
explanation.definitionFit: Flippant means treating serious things with inappropriate levity, so it is less than serious.

clue.text: Brought up a lot of vegetarian food, sadly

indicators.note: in a down entry, bringing something up means reading it from bottom to top
a lot of something is most but not all of it, so its last letter is dropped

parts.note: a salad is a typical meat-free dish

explanation.surface: Someone sadly threw up most of their salad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Brought up' suggests vomiting, but it signals reversal in this down light.
explanation.definitionFit: Alas is an exclamation of sorrow, used where we might say sadly or unfortunately.

clue.text: Text for you in America left in the normal way

definitions.note: a noun phrase: the usual is one's normal habit

indicators.note: one thing in another is placed inside it

parts.note: USA is the United States of America
in text messages you is written as U
L is the abbreviation for left

explanation.surface: Texting 'u' for 'you', as Americans do, has become normal.
explanation.definitionFit: As a noun, 'the usual' means the customary practice, one's normal way of doing things.

clue.text: American state university upheld capital item

parts.note: U is the abbreviation for university

indicators.note: in a down entry, something held up is turned to read bottom to top

parts.note: capital here means the head, so a capital item is headgear

explanation.surface: A state university upholds a key piece of its heritage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Capital' looks like the state capital, but it means of the head.
explanation.definitionFit: Utah is one of the fifty United States, with Salt Lake City as its capital.

clue.text: Problem with area housing the Spanish source of caviar

indicators.note: something housing another holds it inside

parts.note: a bug is a fault or problem
el is Spanish for the
A is the abbreviation for area

explanation.surface: A local problem affecting Spanish caviar production.
explanation.definitionFit: The beluga is a large sturgeon whose roe is the most prized caviar.

clue.text: TV and press perhaps rubbish backing negotiation specialist

parts.note: television and newspapers are examples of the media

indicators.note: something backing up moves backwards, so the word is read in reverse

parts.note: rot means nonsense

explanation.surface: Television and newspapers, perhaps, talking nonsense in support of a negotiator.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Backing' looks like support, but it turns the rubbish round.
explanation.definitionFit: A mediator is a neutral party who helps opposing sides negotiate an agreement.
